8.title: Why ratios depend on the angle
8.prompt: Explain all six ratios in a right triangle and why enlarging the triangle does not change them.
solution: For an acute reference angle, sin=opposite/hypotenuse, cos=adjacent/hypotenuse, tan=opposite/adjacent.
cosec=hypotenuse/opposite, sec=hypotenuse/adjacent, cot=adjacent/opposite. Opposite and adjacent swap when the reference angle changes.
Dividing sine by cosine gives tan A=sin A/cos A; likewise cot A=cos A/sin A. The reciprocal pairs multiply to1 wherever they are defined.
Right triangles sharing an acute angle are similar by AA, so corresponding side ratios are the same. Therefore the ratios depend on the angle, not the triangle’s size.

10.title: Sides around an incircle
10.prompt: Triangle ABC circumscribes a circle of radius 4 cm. It touches BC at D, with BD=8 cm and DC=6 cm. Find AB, AC.
solution: Let the equal tangent lengths from A be x. Then AB=x+8, AC=x+6 and BC=14. Semiperimeter s=x+14.
The area is rs=4(x+14), since the three triangles from the centre have altitude 4. Heron’s formula gives area²=s(s−AB)(s−AC)(s−BC)=(x+14)×6×8×x.
Equate squares:16(x+14)²=48 x(x+14). Since x+14>0, divide to get x+14=3 x, so x=7.
AB=15 cm and AC=13 cm. The area is 84 cm² and s=21, confirming r=84/21=4.
